title: The maturity phases of running evals — Phil Hetzel, Braintrust
talk_summary: Phil Hetzel of Braintrust lays out four maturity phases for agent evals: vibe-checking with documented human thumbs-up/down plus justification, scaling that knowledge into LLM-as-judge and deterministic scorers, accounting for tool-call/CRUD complexity via full traces and mocked external state, and advanced production-trace flywheels. Core message: evals are not exhaustive unit tests but targeted failure-mode probes, and LLM judges themselves must be evaluated against human ground truth.

takeaways.technique: Justified human thumbs-up/down to seed judge rubrics
takeaways.what_they_do: Have a human (ideally a domain expert) label agent outputs thumbs-up/down AND write a justification for each, so the domain knowledge can later be encoded into automated scorers.

takeaways.technique: Eval the LLM judge against a ground-truth set
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat LLM-as-judge outputs as discrete labels and build a small ground-truth dataset to measure the judge's agreement with human decisions before trusting it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: just because you put a robe and a cloak on an LLM, that doesn't make it inherently more trustworthy

takeaways.what_they_do: Use code-based checks (tool-call count, token count, other objective failure modes) to fail evals deterministically instead of relying only on LLM judgment.

takeaways.technique: Production-trace flywheel into offline eval set
takeaways.what_they_do: Capture real production agent traces, identify failures via human or automated tooling, feed those examples back into an offline eval set, and rerun to guide improvements.
takeaways.evidence_quote: don't think about evals as running tests. Think about evals like rerunning production

takeaways.technique: Encode external system state inside the trace
takeaways.what_they_do: Because agent traces can be arbitrarily large, cram system state (e.g. DB/vector-store state at input time) into the trace and inject it into the eval task instead of rebuilding full test infrastructure; use timestamp/version queries where supported.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if a trace can be arbitrarily large, you can actually cram in a ton of context, i.e. system state

takeaways.what_they_do: Start from the agent's known high-level failure modes (from SMEs) and build a small number of evals around those, rather than trying to enumerate every possible failure like unit tests.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you would spend all of your time writing tests and none of your time shipping
